exercises.prompt: Write “These are our dogs.” in Finnish. Begin with Nämä ovat. Use koira (“dog”).
exercises.explanation: Nämä ovat identifies several things. The ending -mme identifies our ownership.

exercises.targetSkill: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.
Use ovat with several things, independently of how many people own them.
Meidän is the personal owner form of me; it selects -mme.
koirat (“dogs”) loses its plural -t before -mme: koira + -mme = koiramme.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -mme: use koiramme.
Keep the possessive ending -mme even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Meidän needs -mme; changing the ending changes the owner.
These are several things: Nämä needs ovat, regardless of the number of owners.
